key_insight: Trial-level auditory oddball ERP waveforms, paired with deep learning, classified schizophrenia vs healthy controls better than conventional ERP summary features.
clinical_relevance: This suggests EEG waveform-based machine learning could help develop objective, individual-level biomarkers for schizophrenia-related neural processing, but it is not a standalone diagnostic tool.
method: 258 people with schizophrenia and 142 healthy controls completed an auditory duration oddball EEG task.
Trial-level mismatch waveforms were created from deviant trials after subtracting each participant’s standard response.
Five deep learning models were compared with classical models using 18 ERP summary features after demographic residualization in training only.
evidence_signal: On a held-out test set, deep learning achieved AUROC 0.797-0.857 versus 0.705-0.720 for classical feature-based models.
watch_item: Performance came from a fixed split in a single dataset, so external validation across sites, devices, and populations is still needed.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Individual-Level Classification of Schizophrenia Versus Healthy Controls from Trial-Level Auditory Oddball ERP Waveforms
